newsitem.title: USA: Mubarak seeks summit guarantees - foreign minister.
newsitem.headline: Mubarak seeks summit guarantees - foreign minister.

text.p: Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak is reluctant to attend a Middle East peace summit in Washington unless there are clear goals and Israel is prepared to abide by previous agreements, his foreign minister said on Sunday.
Foreign Minister Amr Moussa told American television that Mubarak's presence at a summit in Washington was being explored in diplomatic contacts.
U.S. President Bill Clinton on Sunday announced a summit, expected for Tuesday, involving Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, Palestinian President Yasser Arafat and King Hussein of Jordan.
"President Mubarak has previous commitments. Contacts are being undertaken to see if it is possible for the Egyptian president to be present," Moussa said on CBS Television's "Face the Nation".
He said it was not just a question of Mubarak's presence, but the policy of the summit -- "what exactly are the goals of the meeting and what are the results."
Moussa, who described the peace process as "fragile and teetering", indicated that for Mubarak to attend, Egypt required Israel's commitment to implement previous agreements.

"We call on the U.S. to continue to ensure the peace process is back and this can't be ensured without a clear commitment by Netanyahu that he will heed all the agreements and implement all the documents," he added.

"Egypt will continue to support the peace process and do whatever work we can to bring it back on track, provided Netanyahu is ready to heed the peace process and the principles of peace process as have been agreed."

Palestinians and their Arab supporters are angered by Israel's failure to withdraw from Hebron and the rest of the West Bank, to open a safe passage between the West Bank and Gaza and new Jewish settlement.

Moussa said Mubarak was upset by last week's violence and by Israel's resumption of settlements ... "to see things reach this level of insensitivity to the Arab people and feelings, and ... see the policy of settlements back and Jerusalem subject to changes demographically and geographically."
